metadata.provenance: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) Ambient Air Quality Network (2010-2023)

stations.station_location: Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range, Delhi
Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, Delhi

hotspots.title: Geographic Divide: Northern Plains vs Peninsular Coastal Cities
hotspots.summary: Across 130 monitoring stations from 2010 to 2023, cities in the Indo-Gangetic Plains (Delhi: 108.6 µg/m³) consistently experience higher particulate burdens than peninsular coastal cities (Bengaluru: 33.9 µg/m³), representing a 3.2x difference driven by landlocked topography, meteorological stagnation, and dense combustion sources.

seasonal.title: Winter Inversion Surge: November to January Peak
seasonal.summary: Particulate concentrations surge 3.31x during winter (average 118.3 µg/m³) compared to the monsoon period (35.7 µg/m³). Lower boundary layer heights, calm winds, and thermal temperature inversions trap surface emissions, whereas monsoon precipitation provides natural wet deposition.

diurnal.title: Daily Commuter Transit Waves
diurnal.summary: Nationwide hourly tracking indicates pollution peaks late at night and during morning commute hours (23:00: 90.4 µg/m³). The lowest average levels occur in mid-afternoon (16:00: 56.9 µg/m³), when solar radiation enhances convective mixing.

relationships.title: Strong Co-Pollutant Coupling
relationships.summary: PM2.5 and PM10 exhibit an exceptionally strong correlation (r = 0.85), indicating shared combustion and dust resuspension origins. In addition, nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and carbon monoxide (CO) rise in tandem during rush hours, confirming vehicular exhaust as a dominant mutual contributor.

extreme_episodes.title: Historical Severe Smog Episodes
extreme_episodes.summary: The highest historical 24-hour PM2.5 concentrations exceeded 400 µg/m³ (over 6x the CPCB 24h standard of 60 µg/m³), most commonly recorded in Delhi and Patna during late autumn and early winter post-harvest windows.
